process.desc: We keep engagements deliberately lean. One tight team, one senior lead, one shared repo — from kickoff to launch.
process.step1Desc: Deep-dive workshops, technical audits, and a written scope you actually understand.
process.step2Desc: Low-fi → hi-fi in Figma with a real design system, not a mood board.
process.step3Desc: Weekly production releases. You watch it come alive in staging every Friday.
process.step4Desc: Post-launch: performance, SEO, paid, analytics, and iterative product bets.
process.desc2: The person who decides is always in the room. No approval chain, no account manager in between — you talk directly to the person writing the code.
process.desc3: Progress is measured by a link you can open, not by a slide. When the project ends the repo, infrastructure, domain and documentation stay with you; nothing locks you in.
process.flowAlt: Four-stage process flow: Discover, Design, Build, Grow. Each stage feeds the next, with a weekly release loop back from Build.

sss.title: What people ask
sss.desc: The questions that come up most often about code ownership, tracking progress and support. Answers are short; anything that needs detail we settle in a call.
sss.kalanSoruDesc: Write your question and I'll reply the same day.

s1.soru: Who owns the source code once the project ends?
s1.cevap: You do, entirely. The Git repository, database access, server credentials and documentation are handed over. Nothing stays tied to me; you can continue with another team if you want to.

s2.soru: How do I follow the development process?
s2.cevap: A client panel is opened for your project. Stages, finished work and what comes next are visible there, and you get a notification on significant progress. A separate test address lets you see the running version yourself.

s3.soru: Can you take over our existing site or software?
s3.cevap: Yes. I first review the code and infrastructure and write up its actual state — what can be repaired and what would be cheaper to rewrite. We decide together after that.

s4.soru: How does maintenance and support work after launch?
s4.cevap: It depends on the package. On the infrastructure and system management package, servers, updates and monitoring are on me; on smaller packages, post-handover support is billed hourly. We settle the right scope in the discovery call.

s5.soru: How long does a project take?
s5.cevap: It depends on scope, so I don't give a date before we talk. After the discovery step you get a written plan broken into stages, and the timeline becomes concrete there. If the plan changes, you hear it with the reason.

s6.cevap: We work in stages and invoice as each stage is delivered. Invoices appear in the client panel. The payment method and schedule are written into the contract, so no line item appears out of nowhere.
